summary: Exato is a growing customer-experience integration and licence/services business with emerging proprietary software, not yet a proven high-cash-conversion software compounder. Revenue expansion and customer access are real strengths; concentrated customers, OEM dependence and development cash consumption are the decisive risks. At the 19 October secondary close of ₹698, the linked base returns 11.55% annually versus a 15% hurdle. BQS 5.8, GQS 5.0 after the persistent cash-conversion cap, IAS 4.8. Classification: weak setup / value-trap risk under the framework matrix, not a finding that the company is fraudulent or inevitably impaired. Better collections and funded product monetization, or a lower price, would change the setup. [S1][S2][S4][S12]
score_note: GQS capped at 5 for persistent weak operating cash realization. Scores are judgment heuristics; IAS uses a ₹5 lakh illustrative liquidity reference.

gates.reason: Adequate disclosure, ordinary RPTs and unmodified audit; procedural correction and bounded tax issues require follow-through, not a severe integrity finding.

Core P&L and balance stocks reconcile; CF subtotal labeling is arithmetic-reconcilable. FY2025 restated/comparative classifications, development estimates and unaudited foreign components bound confidence without proving unreliability.
Base and bear funded with existing available cash and eligible IPO pots; combined severe collection/refinancing stress unfinanced. No assumed fresh facility or rescue equity.
60 secondary observed sessions and 500-share lot support coarse historical implementation; lock-in, depth and BSE restrictions must be checked before trading. No suspension inferred.

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Exato Technologies Limited, BSE SME 544626, ISIN INE1E4401010; research cutoff 20 October 2026, market endpoint 19 October. Consolidated Indian Accounting Standards of the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules (AS, not Ind AS). Four wholly owned subsidiaries mean no minority claim in this model. September shares remain 10,065,371, giving ₹702.5629 crore market capitalization at ₹698; the 19.10 FY2026 EPS uses weighted-average shares and must not be multiplied by current shares as though it were current capital. Five-year nominal pretax shareholder horizon to 19 October 2031; 15% hurdle, ±3pp sensitivity; illustrative ₹5 lakh position is not an allocation. Identity/share count High; historical financial, governance, growth decomposition, capital-return and valuation-input confidence Medium. Forecast uncertainty remains high and separate. G1 Conditional, G2 Conditional, G3 Conditional, G4 Conditional: no evidenced critical failure; specific constraints appear in the gate register. [S1][S3][S5][S12]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical factor scores: GOV 6, MOAT 5, REV 8, DUR 7, CAP 6, CASH 3, BAL 6, EXEC 6, EARN 5; IAS R 4, D 4, P 4, L 7. BQS raw/final 5.8400; GQS raw 6.5500 capped at 5 because the cash weakness persists across years; IAS raw/final 4.7600. All original weights retained, all factor evidence Medium, coverage 100%. These are research heuristics, not validated return forecasts. REV raw CAGR band 9 is capped at 8 because there are four relevant comparable observations and Medium confidence. Moving MOAT and CAP one point each moves BQS by up to 0.32 and IAS quality contribution by 0.08; moving D and P one point changes IAS by 0.30. Nearby ranks should be treated as judgment ties. [S1][S2][S12]

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: Customers buy contact-centre/customer-experience platforms, licences, implementation, maintenance and consulting, with NiCE, Mitel and other OEM partners. Exato integrates and supports these systems; customers include BPO/ITES and enterprise users. FY2026 disclosed domestic services ₹105.1143 crore, export/SEZ services ₹55.2138 crore and domestic goods ₹7.6677 crore; purchased services alone were ₹115.1233 crore. Therefore gross reported sales are not all internally generated software value. The economics combine reseller pass-through, engineering/service work and a still-developing own-product layer. Management described 150-plus clients and more than 70% of June revenue from BPO/ITES, but a broad client count does not negate concentration in revenue. Revenue must turn into customer receipts while OEM suppliers and development staff are paid. [S1 notes 19–22][S4]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Potential moat: integration knowledge and installed workflows → repeated engagements and 20 large multi-year contracts per management → switching disruption and renewal opportunity → failure if customers/OEMs internalize work, competitors offer better terms, or technologies change. Top-ten concentration was 88.15% in FY2025 and 89.27% in H1 FY2026; prospectus says no exclusive customer arrangements. NiCE is both enabling partner and a source of dependency. Black Box is a broader global integration/CX comparator; Allied Digital is a managed-IT-services comparator; NiCE is a proprietary CX-platform/OEM comparator, economically upstream rather than a like-for-like Indian SME. Their offerings show alternative delivery models, not a transferable valuation multiple. No defensible dated market-share denominator or verified switching-loss cohort was located. Public product pages are qualitative context only. [S2][S4][S13][S14][S15]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Consolidated revenue in ₹crore: FY2023 72.7627; FY2024 113.9073; FY2025 124.2255 (restated IPO 124.2295); FY2026 167.9958. Annual additions: 41.1446, 10.3182, 43.7703; three-year CAGR 32.17%. Five- and ten-year comparable group CAGR are ND: older standalone reports exist, but are not silently spliced into this consolidated series. The three-year window is chosen for comparable audited/restated group scope, not to maximize a score. Gross value added (sales less purchased inputs and stock change) rises from ₹15.3516 crore to ₹45.5880 crore, a useful economic cross-check against licence pass-through. FY2026 revenue growth 35.23%; June2026 revenue ₹43.6834 versus ₹29.0895 crore, about 50.17%. Latest-quarter PAT is ₹5.6443 versus ₹2.7605 crore. TTM revenue ₹182.5897/PAT ₹18.9726 crore uses FY plus current quarter minus prior quarter, not seasonal annualization. June2025 is management-compiled comparative information, so no REV trajectory bonus. Volume, price and customer cohorts are not separately quantified; gross/net and product-mix uncertainty remains. [S1][S2][S3] Earlier standalone context, kept separate: FY2021/FY2022 revenue ₹34.8420/₹41.9237 crore and PAT ₹1.3598/₹2.1635 crore. These scanned audited statements were read; the chosen consolidated comparison still begins FY2023, so no mixed-perimeter five-year CAGR is asserted. [S17]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The accessible runway is cross-selling CX/cloud/AI solutions into existing enterprise customers and expanding export relationships, not an undifferentiated global AI TAM. August management described a ₹660 crore headline contract total, with ₹221 crore already executed by FY2026 and another ₹30 crore in Q1: approximately ₹409 crore unexecuted, not ₹660 crore of fresh backlog. Contract cancellation and minimum-use detail remain limited. Management guided FY2027 revenue growth of 60–70% or more; the base deliberately uses 40%, then 25%, 20%, 18%, 15%, with an additional terminal stub at 15%. It funds 5% of revenue as software development plus 1% physical capex and 24% end-period operating WC; IPO pots are released only against eligible expenditure. The model is not a backlog conversion guarantee. GQS is constrained by persistently weak realized cash, notwithstanding strong REV. [S1][S4][S6][S7] Subsequent evidence: 31 August work-order disclosure totals ₹22.3704 crore, includes ₹4.5598 crore announced on 1 July, and indicates approximately three-month execution. It is not added wholesale to the earlier call backlog because of overlap. Exafone launched 31 August; September AGM reported two signed deals but no quantified revenue/cash. October Claude certification and the July non-exclusive AmplifAI partnership strengthen channel capability, not guaranteed economics. [S18][S19][S20][S21][S22]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: September promoter holding is 54.73%; 72.55% of all shares are shown locked-in. FY2026 managing-director and whole-time-director pay totaled ₹0.6302 crore, about 3.9% of group PAT; named outstanding remuneration is retained within employee liabilities, not erased. The group audit is unmodified, but foreign subsidiaries include management-certified information and an unmodified opinion is not proof of complete assurance. A 16 September corrigendum revised DSCR and clerical disclosures. BSE imposed ₹75,000 plus GST for missing half-year figures in the quarterly-format FY2026 filing; the issuer says it corrected the format and requested waiver, whose outcome was not located by cutoff. This is a procedural disclosure issue, not evidence of manipulation. Tax disclosures require current-status nuance: the annual note reports appellate relief on a ₹74.98 lakh GST item with effect-giving pending, while CARO still lists the dispute; smaller March tax/EPFO items total ₹5.55 lakh. The separate 25 March GST filing specifies ₹41,046 principal plus an equal penalty and interest, whereas the annual table states ₹0.41 lakh principal. The model allows a ₹0.08 crore year-one tax/fine settlement reserve, or ₹0.83 crore adverse sensitivity including the relieved ₹0.7498 crore GST item; these are analyst sensitivities, not an assertion that relief was reversed. No severe G1 finding is supported. Promises versus delivery: FY2026 growth and Q1 order execution achieved; March ₹28.40 crore software remained under development; Exafone launch was delivered on 31 August and two customer deals were reported at the September AGM; revenue/receipts and the 60–70% growth guidance remain to be proven. The statutory auditor was reappointed at the August2025 AGM for FY2026–30; no resignation citing access problems was located. [S18][S21] [S1][S4][S5][S8][S9][S10][S11]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY2026 reported PAT ₹16.0888 crore versus ₹9.6545 crore latest FY2025 comparative. Operating EBIT excluding ₹1.031 crore other income and reversing ₹0.0111 crore prior-period charge is ₹23.5781 crore; reported profit includes less treasury/creditor-writeback support than FY2025. However, ₹12.7375 crore product-development spend was capitalized; expensing all current development would reduce 30%-tax analytical profit by ₹8.9163 crore, a sensitivity rather than an assertion the accounting is wrong. Future amortization must be recognized. FY2026 CFO ₹1.5295 crore less cash capex ₹13.2884 gives FCF proxy -₹11.7589 crore. Receivables used ₹9.2323 crore and supplier-credit unwind about ₹5.29 crore; capex itself did not reduce CFO. The annual CF line labeled cash generated from operations is actually the WC-change subtotal: 24.4905 - 14.4129 - 8.5481 = 1.5295, and A+B+C reconciles closing cash. Do not call this missing cash. FY2024–26 CFO/PAT is only about 6.4% using the later FY2025 comparator, or about 0.3% using the IPO restated comparator, before classification normalization. Even adding back all ₹6.6174 crore FY2024 other-asset absorption, ₹0.7577 crore FY2025 restated other-asset absorption and ₹2.1775 crore FY2026 noncurrent-asset absorption as a deliberately generous classification upper bound leaves conversion around 37%. These are not claimed wholly nonoperating cash flows, but the bound checks that CASH 3 is not driven solely by classification. Both support weakness; no false precision is attached to a single spliced number. Average FY2026 receivable days ≈83.25 versus ≈87.00 FY2025, while closing receivables rise with growth; Only ₹0.1342 crore is beyond one year at March2026, but FY2026 bad-debt expense of ₹1.2653 crore versus ₹2.2474 crore FY2025 means improved ageing cannot be attributed solely to cash collection. The write-offs are retained in earnings, not normalized away. Opening gross debt ₹21.05 crore includes current maturities, credit card, CC and dropline balances. Operating WC ₹38.8538 crore includes deposits/retention and all ordinary statutory, employee and expense claims. Separate net tax credit ₹0.025 crore, tax refund ₹0.3597, accrued interest ₹0.0923 and legacy provisions ₹2.1084 each have one explicit treatment. Pledged deposits, GST-protest deposit and deferred tax are not credited as free cash. Incremental book NOPAT/IC proxy is 21.76%, not a project IRR; unamortized software and funding-sensitive receivables justify CAP 6 rather than extrapolating the ratio. [S1][S2] Earlier standalone CFO was negative ₹4.1416 crore in FY2021 and ₹1.4295 crore in FY2022, with interest inside operating cash; this is separate corroborating context, not a consolidated ratio splice. Current issued shares 1.0065371 crore differ from FY2026 weighted-average 0.8424207 crore and FY2025 0.7035019 crore. [S17][S1 note28]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: ₹698 × 1.0065371 crore current shares = ₹702.5629 crore equity value. FY2026 current-share P/E is about 43.67x; TTM P/E about 37.03x, not the lower figure obtained by ignoring IPO share changes. A conservative EV bridge deducts only ₹14.5372 crore free cash from market value plus ₹21.05 crore debt; operating EBITDA excluding nonoperating income is approximately ₹24.3634 crore, so EV/operating EBITDA is about 29.1x. Price/book ≈7.96x is not a liquidation floor because development and receivables dominate operating assets. The explicit model rolls audited March stocks forward through FY2027–31 and to 19 October 2031, with tax, debt amortization, restricted-pot uses, software amortization, WC, claim settlements and terminal equity. Bear/base/bull terminal EBIT multiples are 12/18/24; these are assumptions, not peer-derived fair values. Base five-year annualized return 11.55%, bear -16.17%, bull 34.80%; terminal prices ₹288.96/₹1,205.29/₹3,106.83. Base hurdle entry at 15% is ₹599.24, with 12%/18% hurdle alternatives and a full growth×multiple table in the linked model. The reverse case needs about 25.59% constant annual growth under base unit economics and 18x terminal EBIT to earn 15%. This is possible against history but not conservative certainty, and still higher growth can consume cash fast enough to become unfunded. No probability-weighted IRR is claimed. [S1][S3][S5][S12]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The critical failure variable is customer cash realization combined with product-development monetization. A large customer/OEM loss can reduce revenue, compress service margin, delay receipts and leave capitalized software commercially stranded. The funded bear grows 10% initially then 8%, uses a 31% WC/revenue stock, 12.5% EBITDA margin, 15% opening-receivable impairment and 12x EBIT exit; its terminal price is 58.6% below entry. Severe stress combines a 20% revenue fall, 43% WC/revenue, 7% margin, 35% receivable impairment and accelerated two-year debt repayment. It produces ₹18.24 crore funding shortfall; no shareholder IRR is valid without rescue. An operating-reset alternative assumes WC normalizes to 26%, development/physical capex falls to 0.5% each, margin 9% and slower debt repayment; it survives but gives about ₹124.11 terminal price and -29.21% annualized return. These repairs require customer collections and lender continuation, not assumed commitments. Impairment is added back once and replacement WC funded once. Deposits and tax claims are not double-counted. Permanent-loss risk High; this is not a prediction of default. [S1][S2][S4]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Neither outcome is a supported target. Fivefold price in five years requires about 38.0% CAGR and tenfold about 58.5%; the modeled bull reaches approximately 4.45× price only under 65% initial growth, persistently high subsequent growth, a 19% EBITDA margin and 24x normalized terminal EBIT. At unchanged share count, even stronger revenue/margin economics would be needed for 10×; any rescue dilution raises the required business outcome. IPO issuance already changed the owner-earnings denominator; bonuses alone were not dilution. Classification: speculative / unsupported as a ten-bagger thesis. [S1][S2][S4]

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Research checkpoints, not automatic trading instructions or scheduled tasks: (1) Receivables: March ₹42.9342 crore, approximate average 83 days; investigate materially slower collections or migration beyond one year, thesis break if cash funding cannot sustain operations. (2) CFO: FY2026 ₹1.5295 crore versus PAT ₹16.0888; seek cumulative recovery across a full next year, not one quarter. (3) Software: ₹28.40 crore not in use at March; Exafone launched in August and two deals were reported at September AGM; now verify commissioned asset amounts, amortization and external product receipts, with repeated deferral a major warning. (4) IPO objects: June unspent ₹16.6455 crore, including ₹4.2341 crore product funds; reconcile deployment to cash and eligible assets. (5) Customer concentration: last prospectus top ten 89.27%; monitor renewal/loss disclosures and concentration, not merely client count. (6) Backlog: distinguish approximately ₹409 crore remaining at August from ₹660 crore cumulative contracts; reconcile intake, execution and cancellation. (7) Financial capacity: debt ₹21.05 crore and pledged deposits ₹8.895; test repayment and collateral against free cash. (8) Reporting: follow half-year results, corrigendum follow-through, tax effect-giving and BSE waiver outcome. (9) Trading: update lot value, lock-in expiry and actual depth before any position-specific implementation decision. [S1–S9][S12]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: BQS 5.84 lies in the 4–6 quality interval and IAS 4.76 is below 5.5, so the matrix says weak setup / value-trap risk. Growth exists, but the cash override limits GQS to 5 and moat/governance/capital evidence falls below compounder criteria. Research/watchlist, not an eligible attractive-entry conclusion at ₹698. A price around the model-specific ₹599 base hurdle level helps returns only if operations, restricted cash deployment and collections follow the stated assumptions; it is not a buy order or a universal fair value. Higher confidence in product cash returns and recurring cash realization could improve BQS/GQS, whereas price alone changes IAS. All ranking eligibility remains provisional, conditional on stated liquidity reference and Medium input confidence. No overall-universe winner is implied. [S1][S2][S4][S12]

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Material evidence is attached to individual claims. The revised September annual, December IPO prospectus, August limited-review results, latest shareholder disclosure and both IPO-use tables form the primary base. Annual consolidated CF and scanned June P&L were visually checked; historical FY2025 restated versus later-comparative classifications are retained rather than silently substituted. Growth and financial confidence is Medium, not upgraded to preserve REV 9. Sources for cash claims are annual notes 5–18 and 31–33. Analyst assumptions include 30% tax, 14–18% nominal INR capital-cost context, scenario margins/WC/capex and terminal EBIT multiples, explicit debt repayment, no new equity, no dividends, restricted cash exclusions and product amortization. Open questions: exact October cash/debt, customer/OEM renewal cohorts, product economics and commissioning dates, fully reconciled historical CFO classifications, BSE waiver outcome and current market depth. These are bounded analytical gaps, not grounds to invent adverse findings. Scenario and score arithmetic is reproducible. [S1–S12] Later checks include the 31 August launch and overlapping order disclosure, September AGM transcript and 2 October partner certification. Older standalone financials are retained separately. [S17–S22]

GOV.reason: Unmodified primary audit, disclosed RPT remuneration and IPO use support adequate conduct; reporting corrections, foreign-component audit limits and an unresolved procedural waiver prevent a strong stewardship assessment. No substantiated diversion identified.

MOAT.reason: Integration expertise and multi-year customer work can create switching effort; OEM dependence, non-exclusive customers and concentrated revenue constrain control of economics. A platform-partner badge is not proprietary pricing power. The July AmplifAI agreement is non-exclusive and explicitly has no minimum revenue commitment; October Claude certification does not create proprietary pricing power.

REV.reason: FY2023–26 comparable three-year revenue CAGR is 32.17%; value added also expands. Raw schedule 9 is capped at 8 for four observations and Medium confidence. June growth supports momentum but one management-compiled comparator quarter earns no extra point. No penalty for small scale.

DUR.reason: Existing CX customers and multiyear engagements offer cross-sell and export access; 409 crore approximate unexecuted management backlog supports runway. Product commercialization and an infrastructure expansion are unproven, and customer/OEM concentration limits duration.

CAP.reason: Book incremental post-tax return proxy 21.76% exceeds the analytical 14–18% capital-cost range, but large unamortized development and old-business operating leverage dilute its evidentiary strength. Future software economics are not demonstrated project returns.

CASH.reason: Three-year operating cash realization is weak under either FY2025 disclosure version, while FY2026 receivables absorb 9.2323 crore and supplier balances unwind about 5.29 crore. FY2025 recovery is positive contrary evidence, but does not offset the multiyear shortfall; persistent CASH override caps GQS at 5.

BAL.reason: IPO funding and low net debt after authorized-use pots support the modeled base and bear without fresh money; some deposits are pledged and legacy claims remain real. A combined collection/customer-loss and refinancing stress produces an unfinanced shortfall, so resilience is adequate rather than exceptional.

EXEC.reason: FY2026 and June-quarter operating growth, order execution and the verified 31 August Exafone launch show delivery. At the September AGM management said two Exafone deals closed, but product revenue, receipts and incremental returns are not yet quantified; 60–70% FY2027 growth remains guidance.

EARN.reason: Revenue and operating profit both grow and latest per-share earnings rise, not merely treasury income. Capitalized product spending, future amortization, IPO share-count changes and FY2023 MAT credit make headline EPS/PAT growth an incomplete owner-earnings measure.

R.reason: Supported scenario base return 11.5443% is 3.4557 percentage points below 15% hurdle, placing R in the -4 to -2 point spread band.

D.reason: Funded bear terminal value is 288.96 rupees, about 58.6% below entry; severe no-rescue case has a 18.24 crore shortfall and no valid shareholder IRR. Collection normalization and lower development spending can fund a reset, but shareholder value remains impaired.

P.reason: At 698 the base misses the hurdle despite initial 40% growth; constant growth around 25.59% plus 16% EBITDA margin and 18x normalized EBIT is required. It is historically possible but requires durable collections, development payoff and a meaningful terminal valuation.

L.reason: Observed 60-day lower turnover bound implies 1.05 reference exit days, initial band 9. Two-point reduction reflects 72.55% aggregate lock-in, 3.49 lakh lot granularity, secondary data and no observed spread/depth. These constraints do not prove suspension.

Q.reason: Final unrounded BQS reused exactly, with no second GQS contribution.

opening_claim_map.treatment: Analyst year-one settlement reserve 0.08 crore base/bull; 0.83 crore bear/severe including appellate GST amount as adverse sensitivity. This is not a statement that relief has been reversed; interest not separately quantified is covered only within the analytical reserve.

notes: Forecast cash rolls forward from the latest audited March 2026 balance sheet, not an invented October cash balance. The first fiscal year includes elapsed months; June P&L and IPO-use disclosures constrain the assumptions, but no unreported interim cash flow is claimed. No interim shareholder distribution is assumed. Terminal October 2031 creates a five-year return horizon from the quote.

No cash interest income assumed beyond receipt of the opening accrued balance; conservative exclusion of collateral deposits is explicit, not a claim they are worthless. Additional ₹8.895 crore recovery sensitivity is equity upside of ₹8.84 per share before discount.

Opening statutory/employee/expense/customer balances and accrued MSME interest remain within ordinary WC on both dates. New interest paid includes expense in the model; historical balance-sheet credit card and current maturities are debt. Legacy provisions remain fully paid or deducted at terminal.

Software-in-development enters a 20% annual declining-balance amortization regime in the model; this is an analyst conservative normalization, not issuer guidance. All future software capex is funded, rather than treating reported EBITDA as owner cash.

assumption_rationale.revenues: Base40% initial growth is below management60–70% FY2027 ambition, followed by decay toward15%; latest quarter and multi-year commitments support growth, while concentration limits extrapolation. Bear10% then8%; bull65%,35%,30%,25%,20%.
assumption_rationale.margin: Operating EBITDA excludes other income; FY2026 about14.5%. Base16% assumes service/export mix improvement but funds six-percent capex; bear12.5%, bull19%, all scenario choices.
assumption_rationale.working_capital: Opening stock23.13% of FY2026 revenue. Base24%, bear31%, bull22%; severe43% links customer loss/collection deterioration.
assumption_rationale.capex_and_amortization: Base software5%+tangible1% of revenue versus FY2026 cash-capex7.91%; 20% declining software amortization normalizes development as commercially used from first forecast year, conservatively earlier/broader than the August launch. No assertion that every historical development project has commissioned.
assumption_rationale.debt: Actual gross21.05 includes current maturities. Base/bull1.6 crore annual reduction and bear2 crore are analyst repayment assumptions exceeding identified near-term vehicle installment, with maintained CC access assumed; severe repayment in two years tests loss of rollover. No additional credit draw.
assumption_rationale.claims: Every ordinary statutory/employee/expense liability remains within opening/closing WC. Legacy benefits funded0.2 crore annually (severe0.4), residual deducted terminal. Tax/fine reserve0.08 crore base/bull;0.83 adverse is a contingent sensitivity, not adjudicated charge.
assumption_rationale.multiples: 12/18/24x normalized EBIT represent contraction/base/premium service-growth outcomes. Three business comparators contextualize economics but do not validate these multiples. Two-way sensitivity, reverse hurdle and cash-survival test are required.
